title: Fix Nx Fork-Bomb from Self-Referential Package.json Test Scripts
description:
Several JS/TS/Rust packages have a package.json "test" script of the literal form "bun nx run <own-package-name>:test" (or "nx run <own-name>:test"). When nx's built-in `plugins/package-json` default plugin infers a target from this script, it produces a self-referential `nx:run-script` target that recurses into itself without bound if ever invoked via `bun nx run <pkg>:test` — a live fork bomb.

Root cause (discovered during investigation, deeper than initially assumed): Nx's own de-dup safeguard (in node_modules/nx/src/plugins/package-json/create-nodes.js `buildProjectConfigurationFromPackageJson`) only suppresses this self-inference when it finds a *literal* file named `project.json` sitting next to package.json. This repo names its project config files `📋️project.json` (emoji-prefixed) per its own convention, so Nx's native dedup never fires — meaning simply adding a `📋️project.json` with a correct `test` target is NOT sufficient by itself for any package whose path is also covered by the root package.json's `"workspaces"` glob list: Nx's unconditional default `plugins/package-json` plugin is appended after all nx.json-configured plugins and wins the target-merge for any package in that list, regardless of `📋️project.json` content.

Task: find every package.json in the repo (excluding node_modules) whose "test" script exactly matches "[bun ]nx run <own-name>:test", determine which of those paths are covered by the root package.json's "workspaces" glob (only those are actually live-dangerous, since Nx's package-json plugin skips packages outside package-manager-workspaces that aren't next to a literal project.json), and neutralize the self-reference for each without breaking the CLAUDE.md-mandated "package.json MUST call nx to run script.ts" convention.
summary:
Investigated and fixed a live nx fork-bomb affecting package.json "test" scripts of the form "[bun ]nx run <own-name>:test".

Root cause was deeper than initially scoped: Nx's built-in plugins/package-json default plugin only suppresses its self-inferred nx:run-script target when a literal project.json sits next to package.json. This repo uses emoji-prefixed project.json everywhere, so that native dedup never fires. Because this default plugin is appended after all nx.json-configured plugins (including the custom project.json reader), it wins the target-merge for any package whose path is covered by the root package.json's "workspaces" glob - meaning simply adding project.json was NOT sufficient for those packages; they stayed live fork bombs even with a correct project.json target, verified via nx show project <pkg> --json.

Verified (empirically, via safe nx show project --json metadata queries plus glob-matching against root package.json's workspaces array) that only packages whose path is inside workspaces are actually reachable by the dangerous default inference; ~44 Rust math-graph-*/math-* packages outside workspaces were already safe via project.json alone and needed no change.

Fixes applied:
1. framework-core (framework/implementation/typescript/) was genuinely missing project.json - added it plus script.ts (test/test-quick/test-long/test-exhaustive targets calling vitest via the shared repo lib, mirroring the kernel-2d-js and infinite-world-r3f sibling pattern).
2. For all 19 packages confirmed still resolving to the dangerous self-referential nx:run-script target after (1) (i.e. present in root workspaces), added "nx": {"includedScripts": []} to package.json - an already-established sibling pattern found verbatim in framework-os-dev's package.json. This disables Nx's default package.json-script target inference entirely for that project while leaving the package.json "test" script text itself unchanged (preserving the CLAUDE.md-mandated "package.json calls nx" convention) and leaving project.json as the sole source of truth for all its targets.

Packages fixed with includedScripts:[]: infinite-canvas-react-renderer, infinite-world-r3f, framework-renderer-react, framework-renderer-wgpu, graph-manifest, framework-core, compose-js, cad-js-core, cad-js-machine-stately, cad-js-kernel-brepjs, cad-js-query, cad-js-renderer, cad-js-runtime, cad-js-module-aec-building, cad-js-module-spatial-shape, cad-js-module-aec-building-structure, cad-js-module-aec-building-energy, kernel-3d-js, kernel-2d-js.

Verification: reset nx cache (nx reset), then re-ran the safe nx show project <pkg> --json metadata query for all 64 repo-wide self-referential packages - all now resolve to nx:run-commands (zero remain on the dangerous nx:run-script self-reference). Additionally live-executed bun nx run <pkg>:test for 3 representative fixed packages one at a time (framework-core, kernel-2d-js, graph-manifest) while polling ps aux process count every second for 10s - process count stayed flat (no runaway spawning) in all three cases; the commands terminated normally.

Unrelated pre-existing issues noticed but NOT fixed (out of scope):
- Several TS packages' vitest.config.ts include/includeSource patterns reference "index.ts" while the actual file is emoji-prefixed, so vitest silently finds no test files (masked by --passWithNoTests). Seen on framework-core and kernel-2d-js.
- graph-manifest's underlying cargo test fails with a Cargo.toml package-name mismatch unrelated to this fix (possibly covered by today's sibling ticket FIX-GRAPH-MANIFEST-REGISTRY-CODEGEN).
- compose-js's package.json has a "test-e2e" script with no corresponding project.json target even before this fix (it was equally a self-referential fork-bomb-in-waiting); left as-is since script.ts has no distinct e2e command - not a regression, just no longer silently dangerous.
